# kala_customer (Resource)

Manages a customer in Kala.

**Creating a customer is irreversible.** Kala has no delete endpoint for customers and no deactivation flag, so `terraform destroy` removes this resource from state and leaves the customer in Kala permanently. Unlike `kala_employee`, which deactivates, there is no off switch to fall back on.

`id` and `number` are allocated by Kala, not chosen, so creating this resource twice creates two customers rather than adopting one. Bring an existing customer under management with `terraform import`, never by re-declaring it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Creating a customer is IRREVERSIBLE. Kala has no delete endpoint for
# customers and no deactivation flag, so `terraform destroy` removes this
# resource from state and leaves the record in Kala forever.
#
# id and number are allocated by Kala, never chosen, so applying this twice
# creates two customers. Adopt an existing one with `terraform import`.
resource "kala_customer" "bag_end" {
  company = "Bag End Ltd" # required: a customer with no company is indistinguishable from an empty record

  first_name = "Bilbo"
  last_name  = "Baggins"
  email      = "bilbo@example.com"
  phone      = "+45 20 00 00 01"
  address    = "Bagshot Row 1"
  zip        = "2200"
  cvr        = "12345678"

  description = "Managed by Terraform"
}

# Updates REPLACE the whole record upstream. Every attribute this resource
# manages is sent on every apply, so a field removed from the configuration is
# blanked in Kala rather than left alone.
#
# That is the opposite of kala_case, where each field has its own endpoint.

output "allocated_identity" {
  value = {
    id     = kala_customer.bag_end.id
    number = kala_customer.bag_end.number # e.g. "KA-1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `company` (String) Company name. **Required**: a customer with no company is indistinguishable from an empty record, and Kala cannot delete the result.

### Optional

- `address` (String) Street address.
- `cvr` (String) Danish CVR company registration number.
- `description` (String) Free-text note on the customer.
- `ean` (String) EAN number used for invoicing.
- `email` (String) Email address. Personal data -- it is written to Terraform state.
- `first_name` (String) Contact's first name.
- `last_name` (String) Contact's last name.
- `phone` (String) Phone number. Personal data -- it is written to Terraform state.
- `zip` (String) Postal code.

### Read-Only

- `case_count` (Number) How many cases reference this customer. Read-only.
- `city` (String) City. Read-only: neither write endpoint carries it.
- `id` (Number) Kala's internal customer id, allocated on create.
- `number` (String) The customer number, e.g. `KA-1`. Allocated by Kala, not chosen.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is Kala's numeric customer id — not the "KA-1" number, which
# is a different value.
terraform import kala_customer.bag_end 4

# Import is the ONLY way to adopt an existing customer: create allocates a new
# one rather than matching, and the result cannot be deleted.
#
# Reconcile the configuration with what Kala holds BEFORE the next apply.
# Updates replace the whole record, so an attribute the configuration omits is
# blanked upstream.
```
